name: WebAuthn Related Origin Requests
plain: Lets one passkey work across several of a company's domains.
meaning: Allows an RP ID to be shared by listed sites so passkeys follow brand domains. Limited labels prevent abuse.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets one passkey work across several of a company's domains.

fields.name: origins
fields.range: up to 5 labels (eTLD+1 groups) in Chrome

limits.headline: Can let one passkey work across a company's own listed websites
limits.user_action: Nothing extra. It happens when you use a passkey on any of that company's sites
can: Share one passkey across a short list of the company's own domains
Let you sign in on a brand's country sites with the same passkey
cannot: Share your passkey with sites not on the company's list
Add more than a small number of site names
Work in older browsers that lack the feature
limits.differs: Chrome, Safari and Edge support it. Firefox does not yet.

story.what_it_is: One passkey can work across several websites owned by the same company.

marketing.name: Related Origin Requests
marketing.pitch: Google describes a way for one passkey to be used on several of a company's domains, such as country sites.

story.for_you: You create a passkey on one site and later sign in with it on the same company's other web addresses. You never notice anything except that it just works.
story.for_makers: Large brands own many domains for different countries and products. This lets them use one passkey across them all and avoids making customers sign up again.

use_cases.example: A game publisher with separate stores and regional sites lets a player's passkey work on all of them.
A retailer with country sites for each market keeps a shopper's passkey working when they travel.
A streaming company with brand domains for each service lets one passkey open all of them.
A travel group with several booking brands sees fewer sign in drop offs.
A bank with separate login and mobile domains shares passkeys between them.
A security team grows passkey use faster since customers do not need a new one for each domain.

risks: More domains in one trust circle

technical_bounds: Needs the file served on the RP ID domain
